body:
This was not tested previously. ClimaCore cannot upgrade to 1.12 until this is fixed. 

The way `Base.Meta.lower(Main, _)` works changed in Julia 1.12.


Before:
```

julia> Base.Meta.lower(Main, :(@. a = b + sqrt(c)))
:($(Expr(:thunk, CodeInfo(
    @ none within `top-level scope`
1 ─ %1 = a
│   %2 = +
│   %3 = b
│   %4 = Base.broadcasted(sqrt, c)
│   %5 = Base.broadcasted(%2, %3, %4)
│   %6 = Base.materialize!(%1, %5)
└──      return %6
))))

```
After:
```
julia> Base.Meta.lower(Main, :(@. a = b + sqrt(c)))
:($(Expr(:thunk, CodeInfo(
1 ─ %1 = Main.a
│   %2 = Main.:+
│   %3 = Main.b
│   %4 = Main.sqrt
│   %5 = Main.c
│   %6 =   dynamic Base.broadcasted(%4, %5)
│   %7 =   dynamic Base.broadcasted(%2, %3, %6)
│   %8 =   dynamic Base.materialize!(%1, %7)
└──      return %8
))))

```




This package was previously lowering code into the `Main` module. After Julia v1.12, unbound variables would also get assigned to that module. This could be incorrect if the macro resolves outside of the main module. This commit introduces a temporary lowering module. The lowering module is then stripped from the name of unbound variables.
title: Fix support for julia 1.12 and 1.13
